stem: Which principle states that a person who commits a crime leaves something behind at the scene and takes something away?

options.A: The best evidence rule
options.B: The prudent person rule
options.C: The principle of least privilege
options.D: Locard's exchange principle

explanation: Locard's exchange principle underpins forensic work: every contact leaves traces, including digital ones such as logs and artifacts.

distractor_rationales.A: The best evidence rule prefers original documents.
distractor_rationales.B: The prudent person rule describes reasonable care by management.
distractor_rationales.C: Least privilege limits access rights.

stem: Where might a forensic examiner find fragments of old data at the end of a file's last disk cluster?

options.A: Slack space
options.B: The system's swap file configuration settings
options.C: The network interface card's firmware
options.D: The computer's BIOS password store

explanation: When a file does not fill its last cluster, the leftover space, called slack space, can still hold data from earlier files.

distractor_rationales.B: Swap configuration settings do not hold old file fragments.
distractor_rationales.C: NIC firmware does not store file data.
distractor_rationales.D: A BIOS password store holds only settings.

stem: What information does NetFlow-style flow data provide?

options.A: The full contents of every packet, including any attachments and file transfers
options.B: Metadata about connections, such as addresses, ports, and volumes
options.C: The passwords users type into websites
options.D: The configuration of each network device

explanation: Flow records summarize who talked to whom, when, on which ports, and how much data moved, without storing packet contents.

distractor_rationales.A: Full packet capture records contents; flow data does not.
distractor_rationales.C: Flow data does not capture passwords.
distractor_rationales.D: Device configuration is not part of flow data.

stem: Which is a widely used, consensus-based source of secure configuration guidance for operating systems and applications?

options.A: The OWASP Top 10 list of web application security risks
options.B: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures list of known flaws
options.C: CIS Benchmarks
options.D: The MITRE ATT&CK matrix of adversary techniques

explanation: CIS Benchmarks give detailed hardening settings for many platforms, and organizations often base their baselines on them.

distractor_rationales.A: The OWASP Top 10 describes web risks, not configuration settings.
distractor_rationales.B: CVE lists vulnerabilities.
distractor_rationales.D: ATT&CK catalogs attacker behavior.

stem: Which protection is MOST important for backup tapes stored in an off-site vault?

options.A: Labeling each tape with the names of the systems and files it holds
options.B: Keeping the tapes in the same room as the primary servers
options.C: Allowing any employee to borrow tapes without signing them out
options.D: Controlled access and suitable environmental conditions

explanation: Stored media needs restricted access and stable temperature and humidity so it is both secure and readable when needed.

distractor_rationales.A: Detailed labels help attackers find valuable tapes.
distractor_rationales.B: Storing tapes with the servers defeats off-site protection.
distractor_rationales.C: Uncontrolled borrowing breaks custody.

stem: What is the main advantage of anomaly-based intrusion detection over signature-based detection?

options.A: It can detect new attacks that have no known signature
options.B: It never produces false positives once it has been tuned and installed
options.C: It needs no baseline of normal activity to work
options.D: It is always cheaper to deploy and maintain

explanation: Anomaly detection flags deviations from a learned baseline, so it can catch novel attacks, although it tends to produce more false positives.

distractor_rationales.B: Anomaly detection often produces more false positives.
distractor_rationales.C: It depends on a baseline of normal activity.
distractor_rationales.D: Cost varies and is not the main advantage.

stem: A critical patch was installed on a server last week, but the vulnerability scanner still reports the flaw. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The scanner has a bug and should be uninstalled
options.B: The server has not been rebooted to complete the patch
options.C: The patch was too small to fix the problem
options.D: The vulnerability has been renamed by the vendor since the patch was released

explanation: Many patches take effect only after a restart. Patch verification should confirm reboots and rescan to prove the fix is active.

distractor_rationales.A: Removing the scanner hides the issue.
distractor_rationales.C: Patch size is irrelevant.
distractor_rationales.D: Renaming does not change scan results.

stem: Who should approve a normal change to a production system?

options.A: The engineer who will implement the change
options.B: Any user who will be affected by the change once it goes live
options.C: The change advisory board or designated change authority
options.D: The vendor that sold the system to the company

explanation: Approval by a change authority, independent of the implementer, makes sure risk, testing, and backout plans are reviewed before the change.

distractor_rationales.A: Self-approval removes independent review.
distractor_rationales.B: Individual users lack authority and full context.
distractor_rationales.D: Vendors do not govern the organization's changes.

stem: Which backup type gives the fastest and simplest restore?

options.A: Incremental backups taken every day since the last full backup
options.B: Differential backups taken since the last full backup
options.C: A mix of weekly differential and daily incremental backups
options.D: A full backup

explanation: A full backup contains everything, so a restore needs only one set. Incremental and differential schemes save backup time but require more sets to restore.

distractor_rationales.A: Incrementals require the full backup plus every incremental.
distractor_rationales.B: Differentials require the full backup plus the latest differential.
distractor_rationales.C: Mixed schemes require several sets.

stem: When building a case against a suspected insider, investigators often examine means, opportunity, and what else?

options.A: Motive
options.B: Media
options.C: Metadata
options.D: Mitigation

explanation: Means, opportunity, and motive help investigators assess whether a suspect could and would have committed the act.

distractor_rationales.B: Media may hold evidence but is not one of the three elements.
distractor_rationales.C: Metadata is a type of evidence, not a case element.
distractor_rationales.D: Mitigation relates to response, not suspect analysis.

stem: Investigators seize a suspect's smartphone that is still powered on. What should they do to protect the evidence?

options.A: Turn on airplane mode by unlocking the phone with the suspect's help
options.B: Place it in a signal-blocking Faraday bag and keep it powered
options.C: Plug it into an office computer to back it up right away
options.D: Remove the SIM card and battery at once

explanation: A Faraday bag blocks network signals, preventing remote wipe or new data, while keeping the phone powered preserves volatile data and its unlocked state.

distractor_rationales.A: Relying on the suspect and interacting with the phone risks alteration.
distractor_rationales.C: Syncing to an office computer changes data and is not forensically sound.
distractor_rationales.D: Removing power loses volatile data and may lock the device.

stem: Which capability detects threats by learning each user's normal behavior and flagging significant deviations?

options.A: Signature-based antivirus
options.B: Network address translation
options.C: User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA)
options.D: Static application security testing of source code

explanation: UEBA builds baselines for users and devices and highlights unusual activity, such as odd access times or large downloads, that rules may miss.

distractor_rationales.A: Signatures match known malware.
distractor_rationales.B: NAT translates addresses.
distractor_rationales.D: SAST analyzes source code.

stem: During an outage, an engineer changed a server's configuration directly to restore service. What should happen afterward?

options.A: Nothing, since the outage has been resolved
options.B: Revert the change immediately, even if the outage returns
options.C: Leave the change undocumented, since it was an emergency
options.D: Record it and update the baseline or configuration code, or revert it

explanation: Emergency changes must still be recorded and reviewed. The baseline or infrastructure code should be updated or the change reversed, or drift will creep in.

distractor_rationales.A: Undocumented changes cause drift and surprises.
distractor_rationales.B: Blind reversion could restart the outage.
distractor_rationales.C: Emergencies do not remove the need for records.

stem: A master encryption key is divided so that three custodians each hold one part, and no single custodian knows the whole key. What is this control called?

options.A: Split knowledge
options.B: Job rotation
options.C: Mandatory vacation
options.D: Least privilege

explanation: Split knowledge ensures no one person has the complete secret. It is often paired with dual control, which requires several people to act together.

distractor_rationales.B: Job rotation moves people between roles.
distractor_rationales.C: Mandatory vacation forces time away to expose fraud.
distractor_rationales.D: Least privilege limits rights, but does not split a secret.

stem: The security team promises customers that critical vulnerabilities will be patched within 7 days, but the internal IT operations team has no commitment to that timeline. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Ask customers to accept longer patch times
options.B: Agree an operational level agreement with IT operations that supports the commitment
options.C: Have the security team patch all servers itself without telling operations
options.D: Remove the patching commitment from customer contracts

explanation: External service commitments depend on internal teams. An operational level agreement defines what each internal team must deliver to meet them.

distractor_rationales.A: Customers were promised a specific timeline.
distractor_rationales.C: Bypassing operations creates change and stability risks.
distractor_rationales.D: Dropping the commitment avoids the issue instead of solving it.

stem: A drive from a system processing Secret data is needed in an Unclassified lab. What is the correct handling?

options.A: Reformat it quickly and use it in the lab
options.B: Label it Unclassified and use it right away
options.C: Only reuse it after an approved purge, or destroy it
options.D: Use it as is, since the lab is inside the same building

explanation: Moving media to a lower classification requires approved sanitization, and many policies simply require destruction. A quick format leaves data recoverable.

distractor_rationales.A: Reformatting does not remove data.
distractor_rationales.B: Relabeling does not change the contents.
distractor_rationales.D: Location does not change classification.

stem: A hacking group publicly announces it will attack companies in the retailer's industry next week. For the retailer, what is this announcement?

options.A: An indicator that an incident has already occurred
options.B: A confirmed incident requiring containment
options.C: A false positive from the intrusion detection system
options.D: A precursor that an incident may occur

explanation: A precursor suggests an incident may happen in the future. An indicator suggests one may have occurred or be under way.

distractor_rationales.A: Nothing has happened yet, so it is not an indicator.
distractor_rationales.B: There is no confirmed incident.
distractor_rationales.C: The announcement is not an IDS alert.

stem: A security team plants a fake administrator credential in a configuration file that no legitimate process uses. What is the purpose?

options.A: To trigger an alert if anyone tries to use it
options.B: To give administrators a backup login if they forget their password
options.C: To slow down legitimate users who read the file
options.D: To store the real administrator password in a hidden place

explanation: A honeytoken has no legitimate use, so any attempt to use it signals an intruder with high confidence.

distractor_rationales.B: A fake credential is not a real backup login.
distractor_rationales.C: It has no effect on legitimate users.
distractor_rationales.D: It is a decoy, not the real password.

stem: A post-implementation review found that a network change quietly removed a firewall rule that blocked access to a database. What should the organization change in its process?

options.A: Stop doing post-implementation reviews, since they only ever find new problems
options.B: Include security review in the CAB for changes that affect security controls
options.C: Ban all network changes for the rest of the year
options.D: Ask engineers to be more careful without changing any process

explanation: Changes that touch security controls need security input before approval. Post-implementation reviews then confirm nothing was weakened.

distractor_rationales.A: Reviews found the problem; they are valuable.
distractor_rationales.C: A change ban is impractical.
distractor_rationales.D: Relying on care without process change will repeat the mistake.

stem: Backups were encrypted, but the only copy of the encryption key was on the backup server, which ransomware also encrypted. What should the design include?

options.A: A shorter encryption key that is easier to remember
options.B: Unencrypted backups, so no key is ever needed
options.C: Key escrow or storage separate from the backup system
options.D: A second copy of the key saved on the same backup server

explanation: Keys must survive the loss of the systems they protect. Storing them in a separate key management service or escrow keeps backups recoverable.

distractor_rationales.A: Shorter keys weaken encryption.
distractor_rationales.B: Unencrypted backups expose data.
distractor_rationales.D: A copy on the same server is lost with it.

stem: After a data center loss, teams begin restoring business applications first, but none work because authentication and DNS are still down. What should the DR plan have specified?

options.A: Restoring applications in alphabetical order
options.B: Letting each team restore its systems whenever it is ready
options.C: Restoring the largest systems first, since they take longest
options.D: A recovery order based on dependencies, starting with core services

explanation: Applications depend on core infrastructure such as identity, DNS, and networking. The plan should sequence recovery by dependency and business priority.

distractor_rationales.A: Alphabetical order ignores dependencies.
distractor_rationales.B: Uncoordinated recovery wastes time.
distractor_rationales.C: Size does not determine dependency.

stem: A company wants to confirm that its emergency contact list is current and that people can be reached quickly. Which test fits BEST?

options.A: A call tree or notification test that actually contacts everyone on the list
options.B: A full-interruption test that shuts down the primary data center
options.C: A parallel test that processes live transactions at the recovery site alongside production
options.D: A code review of the recovery scripts

explanation: A notification test exercises the communication plan itself, revealing wrong numbers and slow responses without disrupting operations.

distractor_rationales.B: Full interruption is disruptive and not needed for this goal.
distractor_rationales.C: A parallel test focuses on system recovery.
distractor_rationales.D: Code review does not test contact information.

stem: Which is primarily a detective physical control?

options.A: A locked door on the server room
options.B: Monitored CCTV cameras with intrusion alarms
options.C: A fence around the parking lot
options.D: Bollards in front of the building's main entrance doors

explanation: Monitored cameras and alarms detect and alert on events. Locks, fences, and bollards mainly prevent or delay entry.

distractor_rationales.A: A lock is preventive.
distractor_rationales.C: A fence is preventive or deterrent.
distractor_rationales.D: Bollards are preventive.

stem: An employee realizes on Monday that they lost their access badge on Friday but did not report it. What control would have reduced the exposure?

options.A: A policy to replace badges once every five years
options.B: Printing the company's address on each badge
options.C: A requirement to report lost badges immediately, with prompt deactivation
options.D: Allowing employees to share badges when one is lost

explanation: The faster a lost badge is reported and deactivated, the shorter the window for misuse. Clear reporting requirements and an easy process make this happen.

distractor_rationales.A: Replacement schedules do not address lost badges.
distractor_rationales.B: An address on the badge helps a finder misuse it.
distractor_rationales.D: Sharing badges destroys accountability.

stem: A chemical spill on the highway next to the office releases toxic fumes. Emergency services tell nearby businesses to keep people indoors. What is this response called?

options.A: Full evacuation to the assembly point
options.B: Lockdown against an active intruder
options.C: Invoking the disaster recovery site
options.D: Shelter in place

explanation: Shelter in place keeps people indoors, often with ventilation shut down, when going outside would be more dangerous.

distractor_rationales.A: Evacuating would expose people to the fumes.
distractor_rationales.B: Lockdown responds to a threat inside or near the building, such as an intruder.
distractor_rationales.C: DR invocation is about IT recovery, not personal safety.

stem: An investigation needs logs held by a SaaS provider that the company cannot access directly, and the provider deletes them after 30 days. What should the company do FIRST?

options.A: Send the provider a preservation request through counsel and follow the contract terms
options.B: Wait until the investigation is complete before contacting the provider
options.C: Ask a friend who works at the provider to copy the logs unofficially
options.D: Assume the logs are unavailable and continue without them

explanation: Time-limited evidence must be preserved quickly. A formal preservation request, backed by the contract or legal process, keeps the logs available and admissible.

distractor_rationales.B: Waiting may let the logs be deleted.
distractor_rationales.C: Unofficial copies may be unlawful and inadmissible.
distractor_rationales.D: Giving up loses potentially critical evidence.

stem: A review finds that cloud API audit logging is enabled in only two of the company's eight cloud regions, and an attacker created resources in an unmonitored region. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Stop using the unmonitored regions and do nothing else
options.B: Enable audit logging in all regions centrally and alert if it is disabled
options.C: Review the two monitored regions' logs more frequently
options.D: Ask engineers to report any cloud resources they create in other regions themselves

explanation: Attackers use blind spots. Organization-wide logging that cannot be turned off locally, with alerts on changes, closes them.

distractor_rationales.A: Unused regions can still be used by attackers unless restricted and monitored.
distractor_rationales.C: More review of monitored regions does not cover the gap.
distractor_rationales.D: Attackers will not self-report.

stem: After a log source changed its format, several SIEM detections silently stopped working for months. What is the BEST prevention?

options.A: Stop updating log sources so formats never change
options.B: Review each detection rule by hand once a year
options.C: Treat detections as code and test them regularly with sample events
options.D: Add more detection rules so that missing ones matter less

explanation: Detections should be version-controlled and tested automatically against known-bad events, so a broken rule is noticed quickly.

distractor_rationales.A: Freezing updates is impractical and insecure.
distractor_rationales.B: Annual reviews let failures last for months.
distractor_rationales.D: More rules do not fix broken ones.

stem: Ransomware has encrypted key systems, and the attackers demand payment. Who should decide whether to pay, and on what basis?

options.A: The security analyst who first detected the attack, based on how urgent it seems
options.B: The IT help desk, based on how many users are calling in about the outage
options.C: The attackers, based on how quickly the company responds to their demand
options.D: Senior management with legal counsel, weighing law, sanctions, and recovery options

explanation: Paying ransom has legal, sanctions, ethical, and business implications. Senior leaders should decide with legal advice and a clear view of recovery alternatives.

distractor_rationales.A: Analysts lack the authority.
distractor_rationales.B: The help desk lacks authority and context.
distractor_rationales.C: The decision belongs to the organization, not the attackers.

stem: A holiday change freeze is in place when a critical, actively exploited vulnerability is announced for the company's web servers. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Use a pre-defined emergency path that allows critical patches during freezes
options.B: Wait until the freeze ends in three weeks, as the change policy strictly requires
options.C: Patch secretly without any record, to avoid breaking the freeze
options.D: Take the web servers offline for the entire freeze period

explanation: Freeze policies should include an emergency process for urgent security fixes, with approval and records, so risk is managed without abandoning control.

distractor_rationales.B: Waiting leaves an actively exploited flaw open.
distractor_rationales.C: Unrecorded changes undermine control and troubleshooting.
distractor_rationales.D: Taking servers offline for weeks is disproportionate.

stem: During a DR test, the company failed over to its cloud recovery region and found it lacked the logging, WAF, and monitoring used in production. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Accept the gap, since the DR region is used only during disasters
options.B: Build equivalent security controls into the DR environment and test them
options.C: Disable security controls in production so that both environments match exactly
options.D: Plan to add the controls during an actual disaster if needed

explanation: Attackers often strike during disruption. The recovery environment must carry the same security controls, and DR tests should verify them.

distractor_rationales.A: Disasters are exactly when protection matters.
distractor_rationales.C: Weakening production is the wrong direction.
distractor_rationales.D: There is no time to build controls during a disaster.

references_topic: Security controls in the DR environment

stem: A DR test met every system's recovery time, but the business still could not operate because a SaaS provider it depends on was not included. What is the BEST improvement?

options.A: Declare the test a success, since every internal system met its target
options.B: Remove the SaaS provider from the business process
options.C: Include critical third-party dependencies in DR planning and tests
options.D: Ask the SaaS provider to take over the company's entire DR plan

explanation: Recovery is measured by the business process, not individual systems. Tests should include critical providers, with contacts, failover options, and workarounds.

distractor_rationales.A: System targets met, but the business goal was not.
distractor_rationales.B: Removing a critical provider may be impractical.
distractor_rationales.D: The company remains accountable for its own recovery.

references_topic: Including third parties in DR tests

stem: Technicians often work alone overnight at remote substations with poor phone coverage. What is the BEST safety control?

options.A: Ask technicians to post their location on social media
options.B: Assign technicians to work only during daylight hours in summer
options.C: Tell technicians to handle emergencies by themselves
options.D: Scheduled check-ins with escalation if missed, plus a duress or man-down alarm

explanation: Lone worker programs use regular check-ins, escalation when someone does not respond, and alarms that summon help automatically.

distractor_rationales.A: Public posting exposes workers to additional risk.
distractor_rationales.B: Restricting hours may be impossible for operational work.
distractor_rationales.C: Leaving workers without support endangers them.
